verses.1: And the inheritance went to Manasseh’s tribe, because he was the son of Joseph. He inherited Manasseh’s land as a descendant of Ephraim. He was a warrior, and thus he received the land of Ephraim as his inheritance.
verses.2: And the sons of Manasseh, who were scattered among their families, were the sons of Abiyezer, and the sons of Helek, and the sons of Asher, and the sons of Zebulun, and the sons of Gilead. These were the sons of Manasseh, son of Joseph, mentioned in their genealogies.
verses.3: And Lezlafahad, son of Hefar, son of Gilad, son of Makir, son of Menasheh… He had no sons, only daughters. And these were the names of his daughters: Machala, Neva, Hagala, and Tiraza.
verses.4: And they came before Elazar the priest, and before Joshua ben Nun, and before the leaders. They said, “The LORD has commanded Moses to give us a land to live in within our brothers’ homes.” And so, by the command of the LORD, they were given a land to live in within their fathers’ homes.
verses.5: And only twelve of Manasseh’s soldiers fell from the land of Gilad and Bashan, those who were killed by the enemy forces.
verses.6: For the daughters of Manasseh were born within his territory. And the land of Gilad belonged to the remaining descendants of Manasseh.
verses.7: And there was a border along the path that led from the place where the water flowed over Shechem’s walls. This border extended to the right side, towards those who lived in Ein Tapuh.
verses.8: Menahe’s land was a place of prosperity and growth, extending all the way to Menahe’s borders.
verses.9: And the border descended to the river Kanaan Negebah, to the river Arim. These cities were located within the territory of Menashe. The border of Menashe stretched from Tzefon to the river. And its outlets became very numerous.
verses.10: It was elevated to the heights of Efrayim, and it became a place of sight for Manasseh. The sea became its boundary. And when they were attacked from above, and in Yishshakar from the north.
verses.11: And Manasseh ruled over Issachar, Asher, Dan, and their daughters. He also ruled over Zebulun, Naphtali, and their daughters. He also ruled over Ephraim, Benjamin, and their daughters. He also ruled over Judah, Simeon, and their daughters. And he ruled over Issachar, Zebulun, Dan, and their daughters. In total, there were six tribes under his rule.
verses.12: And the sons of Manasseh were unable to take possession of these cities. So the Canaanites took over this land instead.
verses.13: And it happened that the sons of Israel became stronger. They gave the Canaanites over to Mas and his descendants, but they did not inherit anything from them.
verses.14: And the sons of Joseph spoke to Joshua, saying, “Know that you have been given a land and a tribe as an inheritance. But I am a great people, until the day when Jehovah blesses me.”
verses.15: And Joshua said to them, “You are a great people. You have come down into the wilderness to settle there. You will create for yourself a place in the land of Egypt. There, you will have healing priests, just as the mountain of Ephraim does for you.”
verses.16: And the sons of Joseph said, “We will not find that mountain. There is no iron chariot among all those people who live in the land of Kanaan, near Shechem and its villages, and also near the hill of Izreel.”
verses.17: And Joshua said to the house of Joseph in Ephraim and to Manasseh, “You are a great people, and your strength is great. But you will not have one ruler over you.”
verses.18: For the mountain will become like a forest; it will be created as such. It will serve as your source of refuge, just as you can escape from the Canaanites. It will be strong and sturdy.
